slides.title: Section 5 · Application — In Practice
slides.notes:
SECTION 5 · APPLICATION — IN PRACTICE
The Enterprise ESRG Alignment Clinic

HOW THIS SECTION RUNS:
1. How the Clinic runs: the group record, the Q1 setting and the non-negotiable.
2. 5.1: consolidate the individual functional scores.
3. 5.2: interpret the Enterprise Scanner by execution capability.
4. 5.3: complete the Collective Intelligence Response Table.
5. 5.4: translate the agreed responses into an ESRG Alignment Intervention Plan.
The groups complete the Clinic on the portal after the teaching, as Capstone work.

HOW TO OPEN THE SECTION:

1. State the section intent.
Say: "This section is your group's Capstone work for Unit 10. You work as the executive team of your capstone organisation. Each of you brings the Functional ESRG Performance Scanner you completed in 4.5. Your team consolidates those scores into the Enterprise ESRG Scanner, interprets them by execution-enabling capability, agrees a Collective Intelligence Response and then transfers each agreed response into an ESRG Alignment Intervention Plan."

2. Read the two section learning outcomes from the slide.
SECTION LEARNING OUTCOMES:
1. Consolidate and interpret functional ESRG assessments to establish an evidence-based enterprise view of the operating capabilities required for strategic delivery.
2. Develop and operationalise collective ESRG alignment interventions that address operating constraints and strengthen cross-functional delivery of strategic commitments.

3. Set the core application question.
Say: "What must this executive team collectively strengthen in the organisation's operating conditions to deliver its strategic commitments consistently?"

slides.title: The Clinic: how it runs
slides.notes:
THE ENTERPRISE ESRG ALIGNMENT CLINIC: HOW IT RUNS

HOW TO TEACH IT:

1. Set the scene.
Say: "It is now Q1. Your executive team meets for its first quarterly ESRG review, working from the annual baseline each of you completed in 4.5."

2. Explain the group record.
Say: "Your group chooses its scribe for this work in the group record bar. The scribe types what your group agrees, and the entries appear on every member's page."

3. Walk the four parts on the slide.
Say: "5.1 brings in every member's annual baseline from 4.5. Your group checks that each function's assessment is complete and records any missing submissions or evidence gaps.
In 5.2 you interpret the Enterprise Scanner by execution-enabling capability and write each finding with its evidence.
In 5.3 you record your agreed Collective Intelligence Responses. In 5.4 you complete the ESRG Alignment Intervention Plan for each of them."

4. Give the non-negotiable.
Say: "No rescoring at enterprise level. Component scores come directly from each member's Functional ESRG Performance Scanner in 4.5. Your team may query the evidence behind a score; any correction is made by that member in 4.5 and flows through to the enterprise view."

5. Explain Agree.
Say: "When your record is complete, each member selects Agree on their own page. Your group's work then goes into boxes 10A to 10D of your team's Capstone S2R® Blueprint."

6. Bridge to 5.1.
Say: "Let us take the four parts in order."
Point the groups to their company overview. Say: "Your company overview, just above the group record bar, shows your company, your trigger, your three problems and your central problem statement. Every part of this work is done for that company and its central problem."

slides.title: 5.1 · Consolidate individual functional scores
slides.notes:
5.1 — CONSOLIDATE INDIVIDUAL FUNCTIONAL SCORES

HOW TO TEACH IT:

1. Step 1: verify the functional inputs.
Say: "Confirm that each executive function has submitted one completed assessment covering all 12 components, using the same 1 to 5 scale and assessment period. Record missing submissions or evidence gaps before you interpret anything. Your team works with the functions represented in its simulation; the five functions in the Section 4 example were illustrative."

2. Step 2: the Enterprise Component-Level Scanner.
Say: "This is the detailed source view. Every score comes from the corresponding component in the relevant member's Functional ESRG Scanner. You do not enter scores a second time."

3. Step 3: the Enterprise Capability Summary.
Say: "The scanner calculates each function's capability score as the mean of its three component scores, then shows an enterprise average across the participating functions. The average is a directional indicator; it does not override the significance of a critical low-scoring function or component."

4. Give the checkpoint.
Say: "Confirm that the detailed component view and the calculated capability summary reflect the same source assessments. Keep both views for your interpretation."

5. Bridge to 5.2.
Say: "With the scanner complete, you interpret it."

slides.title: 5.2 · Interpret by execution capability
slides.notes:
5.2 — INTERPRET THE ENTERPRISE SCANNER BY EXECUTION CAPABILITY

HOW TO TEACH IT:

1. Give the sequence.
Say: "For each of the four capabilities on the slide, work through the three intelligence levels in order: Functional Intelligence and Convergence, then Cross-Functional Intelligence and Divergence, then Enterprise Intelligence and Dependency. Use the detailed component scores to support each finding; use the summary to find the areas that merit attention."

2. Give the three questions you answer for each capability.
Say: "Convergence: which components show similar scores or conditions across functions? Divergence: where do functions differ on the same component, and what evidence explains the difference? Dependency: which strategic commitments rely on an operating condition supplied or controlled by another function?"

3. Name the components of each capability.
Say: "Environment, Operational Readiness: Facilities, Infrastructure, Technology. Systems, Operational Flow: Standardisation, Integration, Process Efficiency. Resources, Delivery Capacity: Asset Availability, Investment, Resource Utilisation. Governance, Decision Responsiveness: Policies & Procedures, Authority, Risk Management."

4. Give the interpretation rule, in the band on the slide.
Say: "A shared low score may indicate convergence; a large score difference may indicate divergence; dependency requires a demonstrable relationship between functions and a strategic commitment. Scores alone do not prove a dependency. Each finding is written with its evidence."

5. Bridge to 5.3.
Say: "Twelve findings are too many to act on. Next you choose the ones that matter."

slides.title: 5.3 · Collective Intelligence Response Table
slides.notes:
5.3 — COMPLETE THE COLLECTIVE INTELLIGENCE RESPONSE TABLE

HOW TO TEACH IT:

1. Say what goes into the table.
Say: "Your team selects the most consequential findings from 5.2 and records an agreed executive response. Each response identifies the specific ESRG component, the strategic commitment affected and the functions involved."

2. Read the columns, on the slide, with the first example.
Say: "Domain, capability and component: Systems, Operational Flow, Integration. Collective finding: order-to-delivery handovers are disconnected across Commercial and Operations. Strategic commitment affected: reduce fulfilment time. Collective intelligence response: agree a connected workflow, handover requirements and shared information standards. Functions involved: COO, CCO, CIO."
Say: "The second example: Environment, Operational Readiness, Infrastructure. Operations infrastructure capacity constrains planned commercial growth. Commitment: increase service capacity. Response: confirm required capacity, funding and a coordinated upgrade decision. Functions: COO, CFO, CCO."

3. Match the discipline to the finding.
Say: "Convergence leads to Coordinate shared conditions. Divergence leads to Reconcile differing assessments using evidence. Dependency leads to Align interdependent operating requirements and responsibilities. A finding may involve more than one perspective, but the table records one coherent collective response."

4. Give the prioritisation test.
Say: "Keep a response when the finding is supported by component-level evidence, it threatens an identifiable strategic commitment, and it requires a collective executive decision. Select the responses that pass all three tests."

5. Bridge to 5.4.
Say: "A response says what must change. The intervention plan says how."

slides.title: 5.4 · ESRG Alignment Intervention Plan
slides.notes:
5.4 — TRANSLATE THE AGREED RESPONSES INTO AN ESRG ALIGNMENT INTERVENTION PLAN

HOW TO TEACH IT:

1. Set the starting point.
Say: "Use the completed Collective Intelligence Response Table from 5.3 as the sole starting point. Carry each agreed response into the plan. Add no new findings and leave the diagnosis where it is."

2. Read the six columns, on the slide, with the first example.
Say: "Agreed response, from 5.3: connected workflow and shared handover requirements. Implementation actions: map current handovers; agree the target workflow; implement shared information checkpoints; test end-to-end processing. Accountable executive: COO. Contributing functions: CCO, CIO. Target date. Evidence of improvement: reduced handover delays and fulfilment time."
Say: "The second example: confirm infrastructure capacity and a coordinated upgrade decision. Actions: validate the demand and capacity gap; cost the options; approve the investment; deliver the priority upgrade. Accountable: COO. Contributing: CFO, CCO. Evidence: capacity and reliability meet expansion requirements."

3. Give the continuity check.
Say: "Every intervention in 5.4 corresponds to an agreed response in 5.3. Each implementation action advances that response, and the evidence of improvement demonstrates a change in the operating condition you identified."

4. Name the three outputs and what the completed work shows.
Say: "Your outputs are the Enterprise ESRG Scanner populated from your Functional Scanners, the completed Collective Intelligence Response Table, and the ESRG Alignment Intervention Plan developed directly from it. The completed work shows accurate consolidation of the functional scores; consistent three-level interpretation; evidence supporting the findings; relevance to strategic commitments; the quality of your collective executive decisions; and traceability from each agreed response to its plan."

5. Close the section.
Say: "Functional assessments make operating conditions visible. Collective intelligence establishes what those conditions mean for the enterprise. The Collective Intelligence Response determines what must change; the ESRG Alignment Intervention Plan establishes how the executive team will make that change happen."

ON THE PORTAL, AFTER THE TEACHING:
The group chooses its scribe in the group record bar of Section 5. 5.1 brings in each member's 4.5 baseline (Refresh members' scores) and the group records missing submissions or evidence gaps; 5.2 holds the findings for each capability; 5.3 and 5.4 hold the response table and the intervention plan (+ Add a response). Each member reads the record and selects Agree; the work goes into boxes 10A to 10D of the Capstone S2R® Blueprint.

LATER, WHEN THE GROUPS DO THE WORK ON THE PORTAL:
Guide the groups through the parts in order: complete inputs before interpretation, findings with their evidence, responses that pass the prioritisation test, and a plan line for every agreed response. A score question goes back to the member who gave it, who corrects it in 4.5.

slides.title: Section 5 Reflection · Application
slides.notes:
SECTION 5 REFLECTION

HOW TO USE THIS SLIDE:

1. Show the slide and read the question aloud.
Reflection — Application: "How would you help your leadership team turn your organisation’s or team’s ESRG results into an alignment intervention?"

2. Say what the reflection is for.
Point learners to the portal section that they will be required to complete with as much depth as possible.
The reflections build the learning portfolio they receive at the end of the programme. Each one carries 20 of the 100 marks for the unit.

Say: "You write this reflection on the portal after the teaching, with as much depth as you can."

3. Set the standard.
Tell learners what a full answer does: Sets out specific steps to help the team turn ESRG results into an alignment intervention.

ON THE PORTAL, AFTER THE TEACHING:
Participants write the reflection in Section 5 of the participant file.

slides.title: Unit Summary · Closing
slides.notes:
UNIT SUMMARY · CLOSING

HOW TO TEACH IT:

1. Return to the question of the unit.
Say: "We opened with one question: can our operating conditions carry this commitment, and where must we build capability? Here is what each section added."

2. Read the five lines on the slide.
Say: "Awareness: each strategic commitment depends on specific organisational capabilities, and ESRG names them domain by domain.
Intelligence: a functional ESRG profile shows where operating conditions enable a strategic commitment and where they constrain it.
Extrapolating: executive decisions shape organisational operating conditions through the priorities, assumptions and practices applied within each function. Effective ESRG alignment requires leaders to recognise how their decisions influence operating capabilities beyond their portfolios.
Integration: collective ESRG intelligence develops as executives coordinate what functions have in common, reconcile what they experience differently and align the operating dependencies required for enterprise results.
Application: the Collective Intelligence Response determines what must change; the ESRG Alignment Intervention Plan establishes how the executive team will make that change happen."

3. Return to the commitment.
Ask: "Think of the strategic commitment you named at the start. What is the one operating condition your team would strengthen first?"
Take two or three answers.

4. Bridge to Unit 11.
Say: "ESRG Alignment grounds the organisational operating environment. Unit 11 turns to the culture through which people perform, and the organisational health it produces."
